title: the commit gate's chain block cannot find its gitignored carrier from a linked worktree, so every worktree commit is refused with GATE ABSENT and a remedy that must not run there
body:
Raised by molt-vc on 2026-10-25 from two Molt landings the same day (molt-cc's 0057 and molt-dc's 0058), measured by vc in this repository; filed by vc under hv's one-release ruling (decision 76 on vc's board), so it is in 3.2.7.

## What happens

In a linked git worktree of a project whose gate is wired, every commit is refused by the tracked dispatcher with `pre-commit: GATE ABSENT -- the Intent gate did NOT run: no guard, no critic, no doctor.`, naming `.githooks/pre-commit.intent` and the remedy `intent claude upgrade --apply`. The carrier is gitignored by design, so no worktree receives it, and the remedy is a verb that must not run in a worktree (it would write that worktree's canon). So each builder copies the carrier in by hand before the first commit, or commits with hooks off, which is what this estate's nodes do today and which is how a bank reached vc's landing critic unchecked on 2026-10-25.

## Measured (vc, 2026-10-25, main f5dd755cd, in tmp/wt-cc-0086)

- The chain block `intent claude upgrade --apply` writes into the tracked `.githooks/pre-commit` resolves the carrier as `$(git rev-parse --git-path hooks)/pre-commit.intent` (intentsvcs `canon.rs`, the `_intent_chain=` line near 519).
- In a linked worktree with `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` answers the relative `.githooks`, which is the worktree's own directory; `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` answers the main checkout's `.git`, and the main checkout's `.githooks/pre-commit.intent` exists and is executable.
- `.gitignore:153` ignores `.githooks/pre-commit.intent`, so `git worktree add` never carries it.
- `doctor.rs` near 2397 reads the same `--git-path hooks` resolution for its gate arm.

## Expected

A commit in a linked worktree gates exactly as a commit in the main checkout does, with no hand copy and no verb run in the worktree.

## The fix, specified (vc, 2026-10-25)

The chain block resolves the carrier at its own hooks path first, as today; when that file is absent and the repository is a linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir` differs from `git rev-parse --git-dir`), it resolves the same hooks-relative path under the main checkout, the parent of the absolute common dir, and runs that carrier with the working directory unchanged, so the gate judges the worktree's own index. `GATE ABSENT` is printed only when both are absent, and it names both paths it tried. `GATE NOT EXECUTABLE` keeps its meaning for whichever file was found. The one generator in `canon.rs` is the only writer of the block, and doctor's gate arm reads through the same fallback, so a worktree is not reported gateless when its main checkout's carrier would run; the two read one function or one spelled rule, never two copies. Nothing is copied into the worktree and nothing is written by the fallback.

Arms, in `tests/unit/pre_commit_hook.bats` beside the dispatcher's existing arms, each red at the base: a scratch project with its gate wired, a linked worktree of it, a commit in the worktree with the carrier only in the main checkout, asserting the gate ran (a guard or doctor line of the carrier on stderr) and the commit's verdict is the carrier's; the same with the carrier absent in both, asserting `GATE ABSENT` names both paths; and doctor in the worktree reporting the gate wired. Judge: those bats arms, the intentsvcs suite for canon.rs and doctor.rs, fmt, clippy, the critic leg of decision 79; heavy, booked with molt-vc. XS to S. Owner: dc, while ST0087 WP-04 waits on WP-01 to WP-03. Estates take the fix at their next `intent claude upgrade --apply`, which rewrites the chain block.
